feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (baseline, 12 mm footprints, 0.7 kg, 0.12 m track) failed on all three development tracks: every trial ended off-track, with max_error about 0.061 m, rms_error about 0.03, and one line-loss event each run. The controller had to use the outer weights of plus or minus 2 to get a usable signal near centre, because a centred line mostly covered the middle sensor. Iteration 1 moves the footprints to 16 mm and lowers mass and wheel track to raise yaw response. Those changes address the single bend excursion. If the next race shows max_error below 0.06 with line_loss_events at or near zero, keep the array and check whether completion comes from speed or turn authority. If line_loss_events rise above one per run, the 16 mm footprints are probably overlapping too much; return to 12 mm and widen the outer sensors to plus or minus 0.05 m. If max_error stays pinned at 0.06 with low line loss, turn authority is the limit and the next step is a shorter wheel track or a wider array.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events rise or the signal saturates near centre, return sensor_size to 0.012 and widen the outer sensors to x = plus or minus 0.05 m. Evidence: iteration 0 showed the outer 12 mm sensors responded only after about 1 cm of offset.

If max_error stays about 0.06 with line_loss_events near zero, reduce wheel_track from 0.10 m to 0.09 m to add turn authority. Evidence: iteration 0 showed every track ending at the same 0.061 m excursion, which points to turn rate, not sensing.

If steering_oscillation rises with control_effort, keep mass at 0.5 kg and raise body_length to 0.20 m, which adds yaw damping through the larger inertia without changing the sensor row. Evidence: iteration 0 steering_oscillation was about 0.07 on all tracks, so the baseline was not yet oscillating.
